manageClusterDesc: Initialize and manage your MaxIOFS cluster
monitorClusterDesc: Monitor and manage your MaxIOFS cluster
clusterNotInitializedDesc: Initialize a new cluster with this node, or add this node to an existing cluster from that cluster's console: Manage Nodes, Add Node.
initClusterDesc: This creates a new cluster with this node as its first member. Other nodes are added from Manage Nodes, Add Node.
nodeAddressHint: The IP address other cluster nodes will use to reach this server (e.g. 192.168.1.10, 10.0.0.5).
saveTokenWarning: The nodes of the cluster authenticate to each other with this token: keep it secret. Other nodes are added from Manage Nodes, Add Node, with their administrator credentials.
clusterTokenDesc: The nodes of the cluster authenticate to each other with this token: keep it secret. Other nodes are added from Manage Nodes, Add Node, with their administrator credentials.
confirmRemoveNode: Are you sure you want to remove this node from the cluster?
drainWaiting: Waiting for the node to answer: its objects move once it is back.
encryptionSecretMismatchHint: This node cannot decrypt the credentials the others store. The coordinator sends it its secret within a minute; if this persists, check the logs of both nodes.
clusterDegradedFallback: The cluster cannot maintain the configured replication factor. Add capacity or lower the factor.
drainDrainedDisabled: Node is already drained or being drained.
drainNodeConfirmBody: Drain node {{node}}? It takes no new data and moves its objects to the other nodes. Once it holds none it serves no request and can be removed from the cluster.
drainNodeSuccess: Drain of {{node}} started — its objects are moved to the other nodes.
scrubberDesc: Scans replicas in the background to detect and repair silent divergences.
scrubberIdle: No active cycle. The scrubber is idle until its next scheduled run.
manageNodesDesc: Manage nodes in your MaxIOFS cluster
noNodesYet: No nodes added yet. Add your first node to start building the cluster.
addNodeDesc: Enter the console URL and admin credentials of the remote node. The node must be in standalone mode (not already in a cluster).
consoleUrlHint: IP address of the remote node (console port 8081). Cluster communication will use port 8082 automatically.
endpointCannotChange: Endpoint cannot be changed. Remove and re-add the node to change the endpoint.
priorityHint: Lower values = higher priority for routing (1-1000)
haReplicationDesc: How the cluster keeps the data — whole copies or parity — applies to all buckets on all nodes
haLoadError: Failed to load cluster HA status. Is the cluster enabled?
storagePressureDesc_one: {{nodes}} is above 80% capacity. Consider expanding storage or reducing the replication factor.
storagePressureDesc_other: {{nodes}} are above 80% capacity. Consider expanding storage or reducing the replication factor.
confirmDowngradeBody: You are reducing the replication factor from ×{{from}} to ×{{to}}. {{desc}} This will remove redundant copies from some nodes in the background.
confirmChangeBody: You are changing the replication factor to ×{{factor}}. {{desc}} The cluster will sync all data to new replicas in the background.
factorNoReplicationDesc: One copy of each object, on the node with room. No redundancy: while a node is down, its objects cannot be read.
factorMirrorDesc: Two copies of each object, on different nodes. Tolerates 1 node failure.
factorTripleDesc: Three copies of each object, on different nodes. Tolerates 2 simultaneous node failures.
factorParityDesc: Each object is cut in data shards and parity shards, one per node. Up to 4 nodes it tolerates 1 node failure, from 5 nodes 2, with less space than whole copies.
confirmParityBody: You are turning parity on. {{desc}} The cluster cuts the objects it holds in shards in the background.
confirmLeaveParityBody: You are turning parity off for ×{{factor}} whole copies. {{desc}} The cluster makes the copies of the objects in the background.
replicaSyncDesc: Initial and catch-up sync jobs for each replica node
storageClassesDesc: Groups of nodes that keep the data of one storage class, each with its own protection
storageClassesInfo: Each node keeps the data of one class. STANDARD is every node in no other class; its protection is set on the HA page. An object goes to a class with the storage class of its upload or copy, or with a lifecycle transition, and is read from any node. An object of a class the cluster does not keep is kept in STANDARD.
storageClassesLoadError: Failed to load the storage classes
storageClassNoNodes: No node keeps this class yet: its objects are kept on the nodes of other classes.
storageClassBelowProtection: Nodes taking data: {{count}} of the {{required}} its protection needs. Its objects are also kept on nodes of other classes.
storageClassDeleteConfirmBody: Delete {{name}}? Its nodes go back to STANDARD and its objects are kept there, still of class {{name}}.
storageClassChangeConfirmBody: {{name}} will keep its objects as follows: {{desc}} The cluster moves its objects in the background.
addStorageClassDesc: The class keeps its data on the nodes you put in it below.
storageClassAllAdded: The cluster keeps every storage class it can.
storageClassNodesDesc: A node put in another class moves the objects of its old class to the other nodes of that class, and takes those of its new one.
moveNodeConfirmBody: Move {{node}} from {{from}} to {{to}}? Its objects of {{from}} are moved to the other nodes of that class, and it takes the objects of {{to}}.
haStandardNote: This is the protection of STANDARD. Each other storage class has its own.
